question: A student records the following quantities during an experiment: mass $5\,\text{kg}$, displacement $12\,\text{m}$ towards east, time $4\,\text{s}$, velocity $3\,\text{m s}^{-1}$ towards north, work done $60\,\text{J}$ and force $10\,\text{N}$ acting vertically downward.(a) Classify each quantity as a scalar or a vector, giving a reason.(b) Examine whether displacement and distance can always be represented by the same type of quantity. Justify your answer.
explanation: (a)A scalar quantity has magnitude only, whereas a vector quantity has both magnitude and direction.Mass $5\,\text{kg}$ is a scalar because only its magnitude is specified.Displacement $12\,\text{m}$ towards east is a vector because it has magnitude and direction.Time $4\,\text{s}$ is a scalar because it has magnitude only.Velocity $3\,\text{m s}^{-1}$ towards north is a vector because it has magnitude and direction.Work done $60\,\text{J}$ is a scalar because it has magnitude only.Force $10\,\text{N}$ vertically downward is a vector because it has magnitude and direction.Final ResultThe scalar quantities are mass, time and work done. The vector quantities are displacement, velocity and force.(b)Distance is the total length of the path travelled and has no associated direction. Therefore, it is a scalar quantity.Displacement describes the change in position from the initial point to the terminal point and has both magnitude and direction. Therefore, it is a vector quantity.Hence, distance and displacement cannot always be represented by the same type of quantity.

options.A:
(a) Scalars: mass, time and work done; vectors: displacement, velocity and force.
(b) Distance is scalar while displacement is vector, so they are not the same type of quantity.
options.B:
(a) Scalars: mass, displacement and work done; vectors: time, velocity and force.
(b) Distance and displacement are both scalar quantities.
options.C:
(a) Scalars: mass, time and velocity; vectors: displacement, work done and force.
(b) Distance is vector while displacement is scalar.
options.D:
(a) Scalars: time and work done; vectors: mass, displacement, velocity and force.
(b) Distance and displacement are both vector quantities.
